## Scope

A mapping declares correspondences between two independently configured reference catalogues.

Catalogue definitions and lookup behaviour remain in the existing reference configurations.

## One survey, two catalogues

The survey model already expects station codes such as `001` and observer codes such as `ALICE`.

A second catalogue represents the same stations and observers using technical IDs.

The model stays unchanged: the mapping supplies the reference codes it already expects.

All example files live together under `examples/survey/` in the installed package.

Download the complete example from [Package resources](resources.html#example-downloads).

### Load the catalogues once

Both catalogues are bundled with the package; this example requires no network access.

Cache paths are omitted, so each source receives a temporary cache for this R session.

```{r mapping-setup}
# Load the reference catalogue and mapping functions.
library(form.references)
# Locate the survey files bundled with the installed package.
resources_directory <- system.file("examples", "survey", package = "form.references")
# Read the source catalogue configuration, which uses technical IDs.
source_references_configuration <- read_reference_configuration(
  file.path(resources_directory, "references-source.yaml"))
# Read the target configuration, which supplies the survey model's codes.
target_references_configuration <- read_reference_configuration(
  file.path(resources_directory, "references.yaml"))
# Bind both configurations to the names used in mapping.yaml.
references_configurations <- list(
  source = source_references_configuration,
  target = target_references_configuration)
# Load the source station and observer tables into a temporary cache.
source_tables <- get_reference_tables(
  c("stations", "observers"), source_references_configuration$catalogues$code_lists$source)
# Load the target station and observer tables into a separate temporary cache.
target_tables <- get_reference_tables(
  c("stations", "observers"), target_references_configuration$catalogues$code_lists$source)
```

The two station tables describe the same sites with different identifiers.

```{r mapping-station-tables}
# Display the source stations and their technical IDs.
knitr::kable(source_tables$data$stations, caption = "Source stations")
# Display the corresponding target stations and their survey codes.
knitr::kable(target_tables$data$stations, caption = "Target stations")
```

The observer tables share names rather than technical IDs.

```{r mapping-observer-tables}
# Display the source observers, including the deliberate data issues.
knitr::kable(source_tables$data$observers, caption = "Source observers")
# Display the target observer names and codes used by the survey model.
knitr::kable(target_tables$data$observers, caption = "Target observers")
```

Missing names, duplicate IDs and unmatched entries are deliberate examples of unresolved source data.

### Read and prepare the mapping

The [resource article](resources.html#survey-mapping-configuration) presents the mapping used below.

The station mapping uses a CSV; the observer rebound reads the source record's `name` property.

The second observer alternative accepts a supplied name directly, without looking up a source record.

The CSV includes duplicate and conflicting pairs so their different outcomes can be demonstrated.

Preparation reuses the verified caches populated above and builds the required indexes.

```{r mapping-prepare}
# Read the mapping declarations and resolve their lookup defaults and file paths.
mapping_configuration <- read_mapping_configuration(file.path(resources_directory, "mapping.yaml"))
# Prepare lookup indexes and correspondences using the cached catalogue data.
mapping_references <- prepare_mapping_references(mapping_configuration, references_configurations, offline = TRUE)
```

Each statement below displays the source value, target value, resolution status and stage.

## Successful correspondences

### DIRECT through a CSV

`station-north` maps to target code `001`; the leading zeros are preserved because codes remain text.

```{r mapping-direct}
# Resolve the station through the CSV and display the four summary columns.
map_reference_values(mapping_references, "stations", "station-north")[, 1:4]
```

### REBOUND through a source property

`person-alice` finds a source observer and reads `Example Alice`.

The target name lookup normalizes the word order to match `Alice Example` and returns code `ALICE`.

```{r mapping-rebound}
# Find the source observer by ID, then match its name in the target catalogue.
map_reference_values(mapping_references, "observers", "person-alice", source_lookup = "id")[, 1:4]
```

### DIRECT with unchanged input

Supplying `Alice Example` directly needs only the target name lookup; no source record is read.

```{r mapping-unchanged}
# Send the supplied name directly to the target observer lookup.
map_reference_values(mapping_references, "observers", "Alice Example", source_lookup = "name")[, 1:4]
```

## Catalogue aliases and matching

### A source alias applies during rebound

The source ID alias `former-alice` resolves to `person-alice` before the name is read.

```{r mapping-source-alias}
# Resolve the former source ID through its catalogue alias before reading the name.
map_reference_values(mapping_references, "observers", "former-alice", source_lookup = "id")[, 1:4]
```

### A target alias applies after a CSV correspondence

`station-legacy` maps to `OLD-STATION`; the target catalogue alias then resolves it to `001`.

```{r mapping-target-alias}
# Translate the CSV value OLD-STATION through the target catalogue's code alias.
map_reference_values(mapping_references, "stations", "station-legacy")[, 1:4]
```

### CSV matching does not apply source aliases or case folding

`former-north` is a source alias, but only exact CSV keys are accepted here.

```{r mapping-csv-exact}
# Show that a source alias and an uppercase variant are not exact CSV keys.
map_reference_values(mapping_references, "stations", c("former-north", "STATION-NORTH"))[, 1:4]
```

### Unchanged input does not apply source aliases

`A. Example` is an alias in the source catalogue only; sending it directly to the target produces `no_match`.

```{r mapping-unchanged-source-alias}
# Show that an alias belonging only to the source is unknown to the target lookup.
map_reference_values(mapping_references, "observers", "A. Example", source_lookup = "name")[, 1:4]
```

### Catalogue lookups retain their configured case handling

The source ID lookup ignores case, so `PERSON-BOB` resolves to observer `BOB`.

```{r mapping-ignore-case}
# Resolve the uppercase ID using the source lookup's ignore_case setting.
map_reference_values(mapping_references, "observers", "PERSON-BOB", source_lookup = "id")[, 1:4]
```

### Normalized names work after rebound

`person-alice-formatted` supplies `Example, Alice`; the target normalizes this to match `Alice Example`.

```{r mapping-rebound-normalized}
# Match the source name Example, Alice after normalizing punctuation and word order.
map_reference_values(mapping_references, "observers", "person-alice-formatted", source_lookup = "id")[, 1:4]
```

### Name normalization is not fuzzy matching

Word order and punctuation normalize, but a misspelling such as `Alic Example` remains unmatched.

```{r mapping-normalized-not-fuzzy}
# Compare a normalized match with a misspelling that remains unresolved.
map_reference_values(mapping_references, "observers", c("Example, Alice", "Alic Example"), source_lookup = "name")[, 1:4]
```

## Unresolved inputs

### Missing input

`NULL`, `NA` and empty text produce `missing_input` before either catalogue is queried.

```{r mapping-missing-input}
# Show the missing_input result for each supported representation of absent input.
map_reference_values(mapping_references, "stations", list(NULL, NA_character_, ""))[, 1:4]
```

### Missing source record

`person-absent` has no source observer record, so rebound stops with `missing_source_record`.

```{r mapping-missing-source}
# Report a missing source record without attempting a target lookup.
map_reference_values(mapping_references, "observers", "person-absent", source_lookup = "id")[, 1:4]
```

### Missing source property

`person-no-name` exists but has no name to submit to the target, producing `missing_property`.

```{r mapping-missing-property}
# Report that the source observer exists but its required name is empty.
map_reference_values(mapping_references, "observers", "person-no-name", source_lookup = "id")[, 1:4]
```

### No CSV correspondence

`station-unmapped` exists in the source catalogue but has no CSV correspondence.

```{r mapping-missing-correspondence}
# Report that the supplied station ID has no entry in the correspondence CSV.
map_reference_values(mapping_references, "stations", "station-unmapped")[, 1:4]
```

### No automatic fallback to the input

Although `001` is a valid target code, it has no source key in this CSV and remains unresolved.

```{r mapping-no-fallback}
# Show that an absent CSV key does not fall back to a direct target code lookup.
map_reference_values(mapping_references, "stations", "001")[, 1:4]
```

### No target match after a CSV correspondence

`station-absent` has a correspondence to `999`, but that code is absent from the target catalogue.

```{r mapping-missing-target}
# Report that the CSV's target value 999 is absent from the target catalogue.
map_reference_values(mapping_references, "stations", "station-absent")[, 1:4]
```

### No target match after rebound

`person-unlisted` supplies `Casey Newcomer`, who has no target observer record.

```{r mapping-unlisted-person}
# Report that the source observer's name has no target match.
map_reference_values(mapping_references, "observers", "person-unlisted", source_lookup = "id")[, 1:4]
```

### Ambiguous source records

Two source observers share `person-duplicate`; rebound returns `ambiguous` and retains both source row indexes.

```{r mapping-ambiguous-source}
# Retain both source row indexes when a technical ID identifies two observers.
map_reference_values(mapping_references, "observers", "person-duplicate", source_lookup = "id")[
  c("source_value", "target_value", "status", "stage", "source_rows")]
```

### Conflicting CSV correspondences

`station-conflict` has two different target values; both are retained without selecting either one.

```{r mapping-ambiguous-csv}
# Display both conflicting correspondence values without choosing a target.
map_reference_values(mapping_references, "stations", "station-conflict")[
  c("source_value", "target_value", "status", "stage", "correspondence_values")]
```

## Selection, reuse and provenance

### Identical pairs do not create ambiguity; repeated inputs retain their order

The repeated `station-north,001` pair represents one correspondence, and every input still gets its own result row.

```{r mapping-repeated-input}
# Preserve input order and repeated result rows while deduplicating identical CSV pairs.
map_reference_values(mapping_references, "stations", c("station-south", "station-north", "station-north"))[, 1:4]
```

### Alternatives require explicit selection

An observer input could be an ID or a name, so omitting the selector produces a configuration error.

```{r mapping-selection-error}
# Display the selector error as text so the remaining examples can continue.
tryCatch(map_reference_values(mapping_references, "observers", "person-alice"), error = conditionMessage)
```

### Prepare only the required target

Preparing only stations needs the target station data and CSV; source rows and observer data are unnecessary.

```{r mapping-selected-target}
# Prepare only the target station table and its correspondence CSV.
mapping_station_references <- prepare_mapping_references(
  mapping_configuration, references_configurations, targets = "stations", offline = TRUE)
# Resolve a station using that smaller prepared selection.
map_reference_values(mapping_station_references, "stations", "station-north")[, 1:4]
```

Unmapped source records do not prevent preparation; resolution considers only the supplied input values.

### Preserve provenance

Results identify the selected mapping, target catalogue revision and correspondence checksum.

```{r mapping-provenance}
# Retain a complete mapping result, including its provenance attribute.
result <- map_reference_values(mapping_references, "stations", "station-north")
# Extract the provenance recorded during preparation and resolution.
provenance <- attr(result, "provenance")
# Display the selected source table, lookup, correspondence file and target property.
provenance$mapping
# Display the target table identity and its published data version.
provenance$target_catalogue$table[c("id", "version")]
# Display the checksum identifying the correspondence file used for this result.
provenance$correspondence$sha256
```

### Clean up temporary caches

Remove all temporary caches created by the example after the last mapping statement.

```{r mapping-cleanup}
# Visit both source and target configurations.
for (references_configuration in references_configurations) {
  # Visit each catalogue configured on that side of the mapping.
  for (catalogue in references_configuration$catalogues) {
    # Remove its temporary cache after all examples have finished.
    unlink(catalogue$source$cache, recursive = TRUE)
  }
}
```

## Configuration resources

See [Package resources](resources.html#mapping-configuration-schema) for the schema, fields and defaults.

## Correspondence sources

### Property from a source record

Rebound follows three steps:

1. Find the source record using the effective source lookup.
2. Read the column named by `source.property` and submit its value to the target lookup.
3. Return the target record's configured property.

- Both lookups retain their configured aliases, case handling and normalized-name matching.
- A missing or ambiguous source record remains unresolved before property extraction.

### Explicit correspondence file

The [correspondence file contract](resources.html#correspondence-files) defines the CSV format and paths.

Resolution follows two steps:

1. Match the supplied input **exactly and case-sensitively** against `source_value`.
2. Submit the corresponding `target_value` to the target lookup, using that lookup's matching behaviour.

The source lookup identifies the input column; it does not load a source record or apply source aliases.

**Repeated correspondences:**

- Identical duplicate pairs represent one correspondence.
- Several source values may share a target.
- Conflicting targets for one source value remain ambiguous.

**If no correspondence exists:** the input remains unresolved, without falling back to the input or another value.

### Unchanged input

Without `source.property` or `file`, submit the supplied value directly to the target lookup.

- No source catalogue data is needed.
- No source aliases are resolved.

## Catalogue matching

Catalogue lookups reuse `reference_index()` and `reference_match_rows()` in this order:

1. Exact matching.
2. Catalogue aliases.
3. Configured normalized-name matching.

Keep these distinctions in mind:

- Correspondence files remain separate from catalogue aliases.
- Multiple matching records remain candidates, even when their requested property values agree.
- Name normalization supports comparison; it does not prove identity.

## Validation boundaries

Validation happens in stages:

1. **YAML structure:** check the configuration, lookup defaults and duplicate mapping selections without loading data.
2. **Declarations:** check configuration names, catalogue IDs, table IDs and lookups against reference configurations.
3. **Loaded resources:** check actual columns and values; check correspondence-file existence and CSV structure.

Within a target table, the source table, source lookup, target lookup and returned property identify an alternative.

Duplicate alternatives and ambiguous selections are rejected; their position in the list never decides the result.

During resolution:

- Rebound needs both catalogues' data; CSV and unchanged-input mappings need target data only.
- Check coverage only for encountered inputs and reuse lookups for repeated values within the same mapping.
- Distinguish missing input, missing source records, missing properties, no match and ambiguity.
- Retain source and target values, the selected mapping, catalogue revisions and correspondence-file checksum.

The caller decides whether an unresolved result blocks a field, row or export.

No correspondence silently substitutes zero, false or an unknown code.

## R API

### From configuration to results

1. **Read** with `read_mapping_configuration(path)`: validate YAML, apply lookup defaults and make file paths absolute.
2. **Check declarations** with `resolve_mapping_lookups()`: verify configuration, catalogue, table and lookup selections.
3. **Prepare** with `prepare_mapping_references()`: load selected mappings and their dependencies, and build indexes.
4. **Resolve** with `map_reference_values()`: translate encountered values for one selected mapping.

Reading the YAML does not open correspondence files or retrieve catalogue data.

### Control preparation and selection

- Omit `targets` to prepare all mappings, or supply only the target tables needed by the current dataset.
- Preparation shares retrieved tables and lookup indexes; only rebound loads source data.
- Use `source_table`, `source_lookup`, `target_lookup` and `property` to select one alternative when needed.
- Selection must identify exactly one alternative before any values are resolved.

### Read the result

The result contains **one row per input**, preserving order and duplicates; repeated inputs share resolution work.

The `status` column explains the outcome:

| Status                  | Meaning                                                   |
|-------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|
| `resolved`              | A single target value was resolved.                       |
| `missing_input`         | The input is `NULL`, `NA` or empty text.                  |
| `missing_source_record` | The source lookup found no record.                        |
| `missing_property`      | A required source or target property is empty.            |
| `no_match`              | There is no CSV correspondence or no target match.        |
| `ambiguous`             | Multiple records or conflicting CSV target values remain. |

The `stage` column locates it: `input`, `source`, `correspondence` or `target`.

Only `resolved` rows receive a `target_value`. Numeric and logical inputs are rejected rather than converted.

Additional details remain available:

- `source_rows` and `target_rows`: matching row indexes.
- `target_candidates`: candidate target values.
- `correspondence_values`: values obtained before the target lookup.
- The `provenance` attribute: selected mapping, YAML checksum, catalogue revisions and correspondence checksum.

Ambiguous source rows remain unresolved even when their extracted properties agree.

### Handle errors separately

Invalid declarations, malformed files, missing columns and retrieval failures raise errors before row resolution.

The caller handles these errors and decides the consequences of unresolved row statuses.
